Su Bingtian, Xie Zhenye, Yoshihide Kiryu and many others have broken under the 10 second barrier.

With Xie Zhenye getting 19.88 in the 200m just a couple weeks ago and breaking the Asian record, looks like he is going to be a decent contender at Doha this year. (Still no one is beating Noah Lyles, of course) China and Japan have really stepped it up in the sprinting department of athletics recently.

Sani Brown is another Japanese sprinter that comes to mind.

One thing that I failed to mention in my original post was how Chinese horizontal has really taken off as well (no pun intended).
Chinese long jumpers and triple jumpers have 4 of the top 20 in each event, with China having the most in the top 20 for long jumping and being second only to the US having more in triple jumping.
I listened to a podcast with Randy Huntington the other day, he has worked with Mike Powell in the past and is the head coach of China's horizontal jumps and also of Su Bingtian.
Real smart guy, it was great to have a look at the coaching behind Chinese athletics.

Another world ranked and WR holding Asain sprinter was Chen Chia Chuan from China also in the early 60's, he was a 10.0m guy.
So we have seen fast Asians before, but not a gang of them at the same time.
That is news.
Like white sprinters they can run that 9.9ish stuff, it's when we start seeing sub 9.90, they can't go there.
With the population that China has we should have been seeing what they are seeing now long ago, can say the same thing for Japan.
We have yet to see a stud Asian 400m man, why?
